chapter: Topsy aftermath, Africa and later career
title: The State Department tour of Africa

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: That's right, with the whole show. See now that whole show consisted of my band, which was six pieces, five pieces, trumpet, tenor and three rhythm. And I had other acts with me which all my band was black in the band and then I had six white acts. See we were commissioned through the State Department out of New York and we toured Africa for five months and was accepted very well. And we ran about 15 countries and 85 cities and that's another one of the highlights of my career. It was very hot over there in Africa, but after all, everybody was over there for a while, we got used to it. But we started off in North Africa around Casablanca, Oran, Algiers, then we went down into Black Africa, starting at Dakar, Senegal,

Sierre Leone, Monrovia, Liberia, Nigeria, Abidjian, Guinea, May 14, anyway it was about 15 countries, all up in the Cameroons, up around Duala. That's up near the Equator. But mostly it was West Africa and Equatorial Africa that we visited and played, did concerts.
What kind of a reception did you get?

Oh just great. Well drums is a language over there, you know, and so you had it halfway made then. But I had an actor with me that blew up balloons, Barney and John Shirley. He could make different balloons, all different kind of animals. They were just terrific. Then I had a singing act, I had a Mistress of Ceremonies with me by the name of Mildred Clinton. She used to go with me on these interviews. She spoke French fluently, and she was a great help. Then I had a family of three, the Riches. He played drums and little the son did, and the Riches sang and danced and played the xylophones. But it was entertaining little show, it got some very nice write ups. I have so many of the writeups and all of the pictures, and just everything, almost a suitcase full of it from that African tour.
So I guess the reception must have been very good.

Oh yeah, yeah, it was. Well, see you almost had it made when you go over there with drums. If you can just keep a little rhythm and play a lot of tom-toms. Then after we got there, see, we picked up on some of that
high-life music, then my bass player, Ivan Rolle, he could dance that dance, highlife dance and that broke it up really.
Is that pretty close to raggae?
I think so, yeah, the highlife?
Yeah, it's nothing to do, you just walk and (HUMMING) ... it's just. You're just walking.
Probably in that heat you can't do much more strenuous than that.
No, no and just walk, you know and you just go on and do it.
So that lasted for a few months.
